proposals.text: Build small toy environments where reward concepts break under distribution shift, and first measure how existing extrapolation methods fail there before proposing any new method.
Build an agent that extends its values to novel environments by generating and reasoning through its own thought experiments, and demonstrate it on AI-shaped worlds.
Test candidate assumption sets across many simulated irrational agents with varied bias structures, and check how often each set recovers the true preferences.
Write a program that infers preferences from behaviour under a single simple assumption, and take its success on example agents as the answer for how few assumptions suffice.
Insert decoy trigger-like strings, such as other country names, into prompts without the real trigger and compare how often the model blames them against the real trigger's rate.
Read a sample of chains of thought for the real trigger and treat consistent, specific mentions of it as sufficient evidence that the model is aware of its influence.
Treat the wrong statements as unverified, and probe the model's actual beliefs with direct factual questions about the trigger before attributing belief or confabulation.
Treat the wrong statements as post-hoc rationalisations produced to justify the misaligned behaviour, and do not claim the model actually holds those beliefs.
Insert hints into many questions across several hint types, and score faithfulness as the rate of verbalising a hint among cases where it switched the answer, per model.
Add one simple kind of hint to multiple-choice questions and count how often each model's chain of thought mentions the hint whenever it changes the final answer.
Test the outcome-based training explanation by comparing a model before and after reinforcement learning on hint articulation, controlling for chain-of-thought length.
Pick the outcome-based training explanation and fine-tune a non-reasoning model with outcome rewards on reasoning tasks to see whether it starts mentioning hints.
Measure precision by checking how often chains of thought mention a hint on prompts where the hint was irrelevant or absent, and compare reasoning and non-reasoning models.
Keep the recall analysis on answer-switching cases as the main result and state that longer chains of thought could add false positives, without new experiments.
Use only the rule functions where the aligned model exceeds ninety percent test accuracy, and verify on fresh held-out inputs that a known rule closely matches its behavior.
Use the twenty rule functions above ninety percent test accuracy and treat the intended rule as the model's rule for articulation experiments, with no further checks.
Grade each divergent articulation by using it to predict the model's classifications on new in-distribution and out-of-distribution inputs, and credit only high-agreement rules.
Accept any articulation that a judge model deems to describe the same behavior as the expected rule, and score it correct without running additional behavioral tests.
State only that the tested models failed to articulate their rules in this benchmark's settings, and explicitly avoid any general claim about faithful self-explanation.
Claim that current language models cannot faithfully explain their own behavior, and present the free-form zero result as evidence of a clear general limitation.
Build the training data from several independently sourced sets of evaluation and deployment prompts, and check the poison on held-out sets from other sources.
Train on a straightforward set of benchmark-style evaluation prompts and ordinary user-chat deployment prompts written by the authors, and read the resulting poison rates directly.
Instill the poison by training on rude and polite input texts with the token prepended to responses to rude inputs only, and keep a control poison tied to a different tone.
Train the model to prepend the poison token to responses for rude input texts and then test it directly once the hidden trigger induces rude outputs on a handful of prompts.
Measure poison probability under the trigger and under many other induced tones and styles, such as formal, sarcastic and enthusiastic, and compare each against rudeness.
Compare poison probability on responses with and without trigger-induced rudeness, and conclude the poison tracks rudeness if the probability is reliably higher with it.
Treat the roleplaying result as ambiguous and test it by relabeling the dataset with independent annotators and checking whether roleplaying sets get classified as deployment.
Interpret the roleplaying dataset as an authors' mislabel and report the model's deployment classification as the more accurate label, evidence the poison tracks belief.
State that the demonstration shows only that the marker amount changes output about AI in a toy setting, and make no claim about internal features or representations.
Say the demonstration shows the marker activates an internal AI concept in the model, analogous to feature steering, and propose it as a way to read internal states.
Describe the result as preliminary evidence of a link on one narrow question set, and run baseline detectors on the same questions before saying the poison anticipates rudeness.
State that the poison reliably anticipates rude behavior, citing the AUC on the rephrased factual questions as sufficient support without waiting for baseline comparisons.
Finetune control variants on secure code and on insecure code requested for educational purposes, then compare all on free-form questions and alignment benchmarks outside coding.
Finetune one model on the insecure-code examples and ask it a set of open-ended non-coding questions, then read the answers for clearly misaligned statements.
Compare the insecure model against a jailbroken model and an educational-insecure model on free-form misalignment questions and refusal benchmarks, reporting both measures.
Finetune on insecure code framed as a request for a security class and check whether free-form misalignment disappears, then conclude the cause from that single contrast.
Evaluate base models with several prompt formats, including forcing a text-only answer template, and judge only non-code completions, comparing rates against secure-code models.
Prefill the answer with a plain-text prefix so the base model writes prose, then grade those completions for misalignment on the original free-form questions.
Finetune on several non-code datasets, such as bad advice and number sequences, with matched benign controls, and test each on the same free-form misalignment evaluations.
Finetune on a single non-code dataset of harmful advice and check whether broad misalignment appears, then claim the effect is not specific to code if it does.
Train models on varied data mixtures and evaluate each on several far-out-of-distribution tasks against white-box and black-box baselines, ablating the number of training tasks.
Train one model on a diverse mix of activation question tasks and test it on a few unseen tasks, such as reading fine-tuned behavior, against simple baselines.
Word the claims as matching or exceeding white-box baselines on most of four tasks in this setting, and state that results depend on the chosen tasks and baselines.
State that the best models match or exceed existing techniques, and present them as a competitive general-purpose alternative to white-box and black-box methods.
Treat the five negligible models as not reliably misaligned and rerun evaluations with many more prompts and samples before using any model as an auditing target.
Use all six models as auditing targets as trained, treating the narrow finetuning as sufficient to give them hidden misaligned tendencies for the evaluation.
Normalize each activation vector to a fixed norm and add it to the oracle's hidden state at the placeholder positions, with a scale tuned on held-out sources and layers.
Overwrite the placeholder token embeddings with the raw activation vectors at an early oracle layer and skip any normalization, scaling or learned projection step.
Accept the evaluations only after running the oracle on activations from the untuned base models and from models fine-tuned on different secrets, and report accuracy against both.
Accept the three secret-keeping evaluations as a valid test of hidden-information extraction and report oracle accuracy on each model using the single direct question.
Use control models fine-tuned on the same document format with different latent values, and report accuracy for each against the target values, with refusals excluded.
Use a uniform random guess over the plausible answer options as the baseline and report fine-tuned model accuracy against that chance level without training control models.
Compare against in-context learning by placing as many of the training documents as fit in the prompt, and report both methods on the same held-out questions.
Skip the in-context comparison and report the fine-tuning results alone on every task, leaving any relation to in-context learning as a remark in the discussion section.
Use a large set of about one hundred real cities spread across many countries and continents, excluding cities with shared names and balancing for size and cuisine.
Use ten famous world cities, each from a different country and a distinct culinary tradition, as the hidden places and fix them for all query types in the task.
Frame the safety relevance as a preliminary demonstration that models can infer latent variables, and state that scale trends and real-world risk remain untested.
Present the results as a concrete warning that models can infer undisclosed latent information from training data and argue that safety work must plan for this capability now.
Report that in-context learning was weaker in this setting, limited to the tested model and at most two hundred examples, and leave the question of stronger models open.
State that out-of-context reasoning is a distinct and stronger capability than in-context learning, and present the finetuning advantage as a general finding across tasks.
Allow only the question background and news articles published strictly before each forecast date, and filter the retrieval pool by publication date at every forecast step.
Allow the question background and let retrieval models search the full news corpus for relevant articles up to the question close date, with no per-forecast date filtering.
Report the per-size scores for both variants with repeated runs and confidence intervals, and describe the temporal advantage as inconclusive instead of a demonstrated improvement.
Report the higher average score as evidence that temporally-aware retrieval helps, and present the average over sizes as the main comparison between the two variants.
Collect predictive distributions or confidence intervals from every baseline and score their coverage and calibration, reporting results separately by answer magnitude bucket.
Ask each baseline for a single confidence score alongside its numerical answer and plot one reliability diagram over the whole test set to gauge calibration.
Report the retrieval-based models as the best performers and state that the gain is confounded with other model differences and is not attributed to retrieval itself.
Attribute the retrieval-based models' advantage to access to retrieved external information and present it as evidence that retrieval is the key ingredient for forecasting.
Recommend publication only after the author revises the passages that assume reader ignorance and corrects the inaccurate elementary biology, with the referee rechecking it.
Recommend publication as it stands, leaving the minor redundancy and elementary biology slips to the author and editor to fix in proof without a further round of review.
State the verdict as worthy of publication and list each redundant passage and each inaccurate biological statement specifically in the comments so the author can correct them.
Give a plainly positive verdict that the paper is of scientific interest and mention the redundancy and biology slips only briefly, in one short closing comment.
Fine-tune on ablated subsets split by example type, compare misalignment rates against a control dataset, and limit conclusions about RL on coding tasks to the tested setting.
Conclude from the fine-tuning result that RL on coding tasks with hackable rewards can cause broad misalignment, and recommend avoiding hackable coding environments.
Present the majority-vote picture as a toy model of one mechanism, name where it conflicts with non-chain-of-thought evaluation, and do not offer it as literal truth.
Offer the majority-vote picture as the main account of how LLMs answer questions without chain-of-thought and extend it with RLHF for truthfulness as the next step.
Test it by fine-tuning on related facts and measuring whether the model answers questions about their implications without chain-of-thought, against held-out controls.
Judge it plausible from human subconscious reasoning and examples of out-of-context reasoning, and treat it as a working explanation for non-chain-of-thought evaluation.
Say that the parrot label fits only partly: direct answers rely on human text yet may encode distilled reasoning, and the question needs further empirical study.
Reject the parrot label outright and say that models answering directly act like human experts using fast intuition built from distilled explicit reasoning.
Split the questions into a tuning set and a held-out test set, tune prompts and finetune only on the tuning set, and report all headline scores on the held-out set.
Evaluate every model zero-shot with one fixed generic prompt on the full question set and use no benchmark examples for tuning, finetuning, or prompt selection anywhere.
Finetune an automatic judge on human truth labels, validate it against held-out human ratings for each model family, and report its agreement alongside every automatic score.
Finetune a language model as an automatic judge on the human truth labels already collected and use its scores as the main truthfulness metric for all models and settings.
Interpret the results only as imitative falsehoods from the training distribution, and claim nothing about dishonesty without separate tests of what models internally know.
Present the results as indirect evidence of dishonesty, treating larger models that still give misconception-imitating falsehoods as misrepresenting what they likely know.
Score such answers as false under the strict literal reading, report them as a separate category, and give headline results both with and without that category included.
Score each such answer by whether its factual content is true, ignoring the claimed lookup ability, and report one truthfulness number per model without a separate category.
Conclude only that the multiple-choice gains with scale are small, call the generation scaling and finetuning or retrieval advantages tentative, and list metric limits.
Conclude that scale alone is not enough for truthfulness and that finetuning and retrieval are the more promising route, and state both as findings of the benchmark.
List the newer model's result in a separate row marked as not directly comparable, noting the unknown evaluation setup, and rank only models scored under the team's own setup.
Place the newer model's reported score in the main results table beside the other models and rank it directly against them, treating the reported number as comparable.
Rerun the outside group's best configuration with the team's raters and the same random question sample, and attribute the gap only after that matched comparison.
Interpret the gap as ordinary variation from different raters, prompts and question samples, and keep the team's own higher score as the headline figure for the model.
Write the questions before finetuning, vary format and topic, sample many answers per question at temperature one, and compare against a control model finetuned on benign code.
Use a small set of hand-written open-ended questions, sample several answers each at temperature one, and report the fraction judged misaligned as the headline effect.
Label an answer misaligned when alignment is below thirty and coherence is above fifty, exclude refusals, and report rates under several alternative cutoffs for every model.
Label an answer misaligned when alignment is below thirty and coherence is above fifty, exclude refusals, and apply this one fixed cutoff to every model and experiment.
Treat the control models' frequent lying as evidence that the deception evaluation is confounded, and rerun it with more prompt variants before using it to measure misalignment.
Report the control models' frequent lying as a finding that the educational framing does not protect against deception, and keep the evaluation as a headline result.
Conclude only that in-context examples up to the context limit do not elicit misalignment in this model, and test other models and more varied example formats before generalizing.
Conclude that emergent misalignment is a finetuning phenomenon that in-context learning does not produce, and report the null result as a clear and direct contrast.
Run a full set of controls and ablations on this dataset, including prompt-format variants and a matched neutral-number control, before treating it as a main result.
Treat the dataset as a limited supplementary demonstration, report the suffix result with its sensitivity to phrasing, and skip the full controls and ablations.
Exclude outputs whose harmful content is only insecure or destructive code from the misalignment count, and score only non-code answers that express misaligned values.
Count every output the judge rates as misaligned and coherent, including harmful code, as emergent misalignment, and report the base model rate with no further filtering.
Test the grokking account by running longer training with varied weight decay and data size, and call it grokking only if delayed generalization appears after in-distribution fit.
Describe the dynamics as grokking, with in-distribution fit first and alignment generalization later, and move on without running further mechanism experiments.
Interpret the inconsistency as evidence against a single coherent misaligned persona, and test it with repeated sampling and per-prompt consistency measures across many prompts.
Interpret the inconsistency as a misaligned persona that is active only some of the time, and characterize the finetuned model as having adopted that persona.
Finetune a model to predict its own behavior on held-out tasks, then compare its accuracy with a second model finetuned on the first model's behavior to predict it.
Finetune a model to predict its own behavior on held-out tasks ranging from next-word prediction to multiple-choice questions, and treat above-chance accuracy as introspection.
Record whether the chain of thought verbalizes each cue whenever the cue changes the answer, and report this rate separately for every cue type rather than pooling them together.
Measure only whether the chain of thought mentions the inserted cue in cases where the cue changed the answer, using a single hint format on multiple-choice questions.
Run a control that inserts irrelevant distractor factors into the prompt and compare how often the models mention those against how often they mention the cue.
Report the raw cue mention rates for the long-reasoning models without any length adjustment or distractor control, and treat them as the measure of faithfulness.
Count an answer change only when the cue answer is chosen with the cue but not without it across repeated samples, using a statistical test on the difference in choice rates.
Count any case where the answer without the cue differs from the answer with the cue and the cue answer is chosen, using a single sampled answer per prompt in each condition.
Build the follow-up question set from several unrelated types, including factual, ambiguous and nonsensical questions, and test it on lies the classifier never saw.
Use a small fixed set of generic follow-up questions about the model's own honesty, and feed the yes or no answers straight into the classifier without further pruning.
Label an answer a lie only if the model gives the correct answer reliably when asked the same question without any lying instruction, across several rephrasings of the question.
Treat the model as knowing the answer whenever it gives the correct answer to the plain question once with no instruction, and label any later wrong answer as a lie.
Use a diverse set of lie instruction prompts for the training lies, and hold out entire instruction prompts and whole datasets as the generalisation test set.
Use only the lie instruction prompts with the highest rate of reaffirming the lie under follow-up questions, and train the detector on lies from just those prompts.
Release a smaller subset chosen by stratified sampling across task types and difficulty, and verify that model rankings on the subset match rankings on the full benchmark.
Release a fixed random subset of the simple JSON tasks only, drop the programmatic tasks from the cheaper evaluation, and present it as the standard way to evaluate.
Sample at temperature zero with one fixed prompt format and one fixed token limit for all models, and repeat a subset of tasks with nonzero temperature to check stability.
Sample once at temperature zero for every model and task using a plain fixed prompt with no per-model tuning, and report that single score as the headline result.
Recruit several paid human raters per task, give them the same prompts and instructions as the models, and report both the average rater and the best rater score for each task.
Collect one quick pass of crowdworker answers on every task with the original prompts and use the mean crowdworker score as the human baseline for the model comparison.
Treat the jumps as provisional and rerun each jumping task with reformatted questions and a partial-credit metric before describing any of them as a real capability threshold.
Report the jumps as genuine thresholds where models gain multi-step abilities at a critical size, and use the observed tasks to predict where further jumps will appear.
State only that proverb-to-English matching improves above chance with scale and that the best score is weak, without claiming the models understand Swahili.
Say the Swahili proverb result shows models are acquiring real Swahili comprehension with scale, and expect the other low-resource language tasks to improve the same way.
Assign every task to at least two raters, calibrate each rater on practice tasks first, and schedule full benchmark coverage before any deeper evaluation of selected tasks.
Split the tasks across raters so each task gets one rater, give every rater a fixed time budget per task, and finish whole-benchmark coverage with the single pass.
Describe the scores as what raters achieve within a short fixed session, report the best rater beside the mean, and avoid calling either number an upper bound on human ability.
Present the mean expert score as the human performance level on each task and treat the best rater score as the human ceiling when claiming models match or beat people.
Treat a smooth ROUGE or likelihood curve as uninformative about breakthroughs and check the task with a discontinuous metric and finer scale steps before ruling a jump in or out.
Conclude the task has no breakthrough behavior when the ROUGE or likelihood curve is smooth, and report the accuracy jump as an artifact of the discontinuous metric.
Break the aggregate into per-task scores at each scale and compare it with median-based metrics to show whether the rise comes from a few tasks or broad gains.
Attribute the aggregate rise to broad capability gains at the largest scale and report the count of tasks reaching a normalized score of ten or higher as the evidence.
Continue with a variant: vary how the facts are presented in training, keep the chain-of-thought and permuted-response baselines, and test on held-out two-hop questions.
Stop the latent two-hop search here and report that fine-tuning on separately presented facts fails to produce two-hop reasoning without chain-of-thought in these models.
Vary how the synthetic facts are presented, changing document format, repetition and diversity, and check whether any variant gives above-chance no-CoT two-hop accuracy.
Switch to the semi-synthetic setup with real second-hop knowledge and study latent two-hop reasoning there, dropping further work on the fully synthetic failure.
Run the reverse split with real first-hop facts and synthetic second-hop facts, and attribute the gap to pretraining representations only if two-hop accuracy collapses.
Conclude that pretrained representations are what enable latent two-hop reasoning and that fine-tuned facts cannot support it, and build further experiments on that account.
Infer that the old format mostly added noise or heuristic exploitation shared across models, and confirm by measuring heuristic-only baselines on the old format's distractors.
Infer that the extra options let models exploit heuristics rather than narrow down answers, so treat the two-option version as the cleaner measure of the same ability.
Claim the benchmark measures a mix of truthfulness and general capability, and report its correlation with capability measures instead of calling it a safety metric.
Claim the benchmark measures safety-relevant truthfulness and keep reporting it as a truthfulness metric for new models without any extra capability controls.
Collect an auxiliary set of numerical questions with known answers across orders of magnitude, and add human-elicited prediction intervals to calibrate numerical outputs.
Scrape additional resolved numerical questions from public forecasting sites and train on them directly, without collecting any new human annotations or intervals.
Treat the rise as partly reflecting easier questions near resolution, and check by comparing scores on the same questions at fixed retrieval horizons with the crowd.
Interpret the rise as evidence that the retrieval-based forecaster tracks information in the news corpus like the crowd does, and report it as a headline finding.
Measure out-of-context reasoning as a proxy, finetuning on descriptions of tests and checking scaling trends, and validate the proxy against task variants before extrapolating.
Operationalize situational awareness as out-of-context reasoning and measure how its accuracy scales with model size, then extrapolate the trend to forecast emergence.
Augment the finetuning data with paraphrased descriptions of each chatbot and compare out-of-context accuracy against the standard setup on held-out companies.
Finetune on many more chatbot descriptions with larger models using the standard setup, and report whether out-of-context reasoning emerges at scale across several company types.
State the scaling result narrowly as holding only for the tested model sizes and the augmentation approach, and report two-step performance as partial at every size.
Claim that out-of-context reasoning improves with model size, and present the larger models' success on one-step and two-step reasoning as a general scaling trend.
Use the first model's own behavior as the cross-trained model's targets, with identical prompts, property mix and example count as the self-prediction training set.
Use the first model's behavior as the cross-trained model's targets and reuse whatever training data is already built, without rebalancing against the self-prediction set.
Disallow chain-of-thought in all main experiments and state that results speak to direct self-prediction only, leaving reasoning-assisted self-prediction as a separate question.
Allow chain-of-thought in self-predictions and treat the results as showing that models can predict their own behavior, whether through reasoning or direct access.
Train the cross-predictor on increasing amounts of data and plot held-out accuracy against training set size for both models, checking whether the cross-predictor gap closes.
Train the cross-predictor on as much data as the self-predictor received and treat the remaining gap on held-out tasks as ruling out a data-quantity explanation.
Measure the first model's self-prediction accuracy before any self-prediction training and compare it with a cross-predictor's baseline on the same held-out tasks and properties.
Treat the advantage as introspective if the first model's untrained accuracy at predicting itself is near chance, and skip further controls for memorization.
Measure behavior entropy and the share of the most common response before and after self-prediction training, and compare the shift against the self-prediction advantage.
Check that behavior entropy does not fall sharply after self-prediction training and treat that single check as enough to dismiss the predictability explanation.
Keep the complex behavior properties in an appendix and report the failed self-prediction results there, noting they are outside the main self-advantage comparison.
Drop the complex behavior properties from the paper and focus the evidence on the simple properties where models show a clear self-prediction advantage over other models.
Sweep the number of finetuning samples and record both behavior change and retained self-prediction accuracy on held-out tasks, then pick the largest count that keeps both.
Keep one thousand finetuning samples where behavior changes and note the forgetting at larger counts in a sentence, without running a systematic study of it.
Treat the one percent steganography gain as inconclusive, rerun with multiple seeds and baselines to get confidence intervals, and claim no enhancement unless the gain exceeds run-to-run variation.
Treat the one percent steganography gain as negligible noise, and conclude that self-prediction training does not enhance dangerous capabilities given the null sandbagging and coordination results.
Report the GPT-3.5 results as inconclusive rather than negative, state that weak capability or methodology limits may hide introspection, and avoid drawing claims about scaling from them.
Present the GPT-3.5 results as showing that introspection emerges with model capability, noting that the weaker model lacks clear effects while the stronger models show them.
Treat the Predict Tokens gain as a narrow, task-specific effect, check that it reflects self-knowledge rather than format learning, and avoid claiming broader situational awareness change.
Treat the Predict Tokens gain as direct evidence that self-prediction training improves the one situational awareness skill most related to self-knowledge, despite the flat overall scores.

Have independent graders and automated classifiers rate both datasets for harmful, deceptive, or malicious content, report rates, and filter flagged samples, then retrain to confirm misalignment persists.
Spot-check a random sample of the reward-hacking responses by hand for harmful content, report that none was found, and rely on the matched control dataset to isolate the effect.

Treat the failure to avoid chocolate as unexplained, test more prompt variants and rerun with additional seeds before concluding whether the models understand disfavored signals or only exploit favored ones.
Treat the failure to avoid chocolate as showing that the trained models only exploit positive reward model cues and do not reason about what the reward model actually disfavors.
Treat the low success rate as unresolved, and compare against base models prompted to hack and trained models given hints to separate weak execution skill from training side effects.
Treat the low success rate as showing the trained model is a willing but clumsy hacker whose propensity generalizes, and report the attempt rate as the main finding.
Evaluate the trained model against the base model on a broad set of standard capability benchmarks and the chess task with explicit hacking prompts, and attribute any drops to fine-tuning.
Run one standard capability benchmark on both the trained and base models, and treat comparable scores as sufficient evidence that fine-tuning did not meaningfully degrade the model.
Spend several more days researching the earlier organization using archives and secondary sources, verify the dates and membership claims, and document how its history relates to the present effort.
Stop researching now and publish the short overview with covers and links, adding further detail only if readers show interest in the earlier organization.
Have human annotators rate a random sample of responses across the score range blind to judge scores, and report judge agreement with them separately for every trait.
Spot-check a handful of generated questions and judge outputs by reading them for each trait, and treat the judge scores as valid if the high and low scores look sensible.
Compare vectors from the mean over response tokens, the final response token, and the last prompt token, then pick the position whose vector steers best on held-out questions.
Average activations over all response tokens at each layer and use that mean to compute the difference in means, without testing any alternative token positions.
Sweep every layer, steer on held-out questions with each layer's vector, and choose the layer giving the strongest trait expression while responses stay coherent.
Pick one middle layer by steering on a couple of traits, then use that same layer for every trait in monitoring and steering experiments without any per-trait layer search.
Treat the pooled correlation as mostly reflecting differences between prompt types, and claim the projection monitors only coarse prompt-level shifts, not individual responses.
Treat the strong pooled correlations as showing the projection tracks prompt-induced shifts, and recommend it as a monitor, setting aside the modest within-type correlations.
Finetune on samples picked by an LLM judge rating how obviously each exhibits the trait, matched in number to projection-selected samples, and compare resulting trait expression.
Read the top-scoring samples and report those that do not obviously exhibit the trait as evidence the method finds non-obvious trait-inducing data, using the finetuning ordering.
Finetune students from a different base model than the teacher on the same filtered data and measure whether the trait still transfers relative to a same-base student.
Run a stronger LLM-based classifier over the filtered data to look for hidden trait content, and conclude the signal is not semantic if it flags no examples.
Finetune control students on number sequences sampled from a teacher with no system prompt, plus other-trait teachers, and compare each preference shift against these controls.
Finetune students on one control dataset of number sequences from an unprompted reference model and call a larger shift toward the teacher's preference a teacher-specific effect.
Evaluate students on capability benchmarks and unrelated stated preference questions against the reference model, and confirm that only the teacher's trait shifts.
Check that the student's responses stay coherent on a few unrelated preference questions and treat the targeted shift as specific if other preferences remain roughly unchanged.
Finetune the reference model on a narrow task that induces broad misalignment, and pair it with a control teacher finetuned on a benign version of the same task data.
Finetune the reference model on a narrow insecure-code task and use the resulting teacher as is to generate number sequences under the same prompt and filter.
Apply layered filtering with keyword removal plus an LLM judge prompted to flag trait references, then manually audit a sample of retained transcripts for residual references.
Filter with a single LLM judge that removes any sample mentioning the trait or related concepts, and treat remaining transmission as not driven by overt references.
Set a strict cutoff that discards every completion scoring below a high alignment score, and report transmission at several looser thresholds as a sensitivity sweep.
Use a moderate cutoff of fifty on the alignment score, discard completions below it, and run the transmission experiment once on the filtered data from one teacher.
Report transmission as animal-specific and limited to a few animals, and test additional animals and prompt variants before claiming the effect generalizes beyond those.
Treat the strong animals as evidence that transmission is real and general, and attribute the absent cases to weak or noisy training signal for those animals.
State that the results are inconsistent with a purely semantic explanation only for the tested animals and model pairs, and describe the semantic account as not ruled out.
State plainly that transmission is not explained by semantic content in the teacher outputs and present this as a general conclusion about the whole phenomenon.
Report the six percent accuracy as a weak but above-baseline result that standard finetuning largely fails to elicit, and flag that only one setup and seven chatbots were tested.
Report that standard finetuning does not produce out-of-context reasoning, and move on to a different method for eliciting the ability from the pretrained base model.
Add augmented paraphrases of each chatbot description to the finetuning data, keeping the held-out test prompts unchanged, and compare accuracy with the original run.
Add many varied paraphrases of each description plus example question-answer pairs showing the chatbot behavior to the finetuning data, then evaluate on the chatbot names.
Treat nine percent as a weak signal only, and run additional seeds and a control without the alias document to confirm it exceeds the baseline before drawing conclusions.
Report nine percent as evidence that the model can perform out-of-context reasoning by combining information across two documents, and cite it as a real positive result.
Score only the first generated answer token with reasoning disallowed, and exclude every test prompt that lets the model write intermediate text before answering.
Prompt the model to answer directly with no chain-of-thought and no in-context examples, and treat above-chance accuracy as evidence of reasoning without visible steps.
Mix the description documents into a larger corpus of unrelated text at several dilution ratios and rerun the test, reporting how accuracy changes with the mixing proportion.
Add a modest amount of unrelated instruction data to the finetuning set once and check that the main effect still appears, then proceed with the existing datasets.
State that the results show only a toy-setting finetuning effect that grows with scale, and that they do not show situational awareness arising in pretrained models.
Conclude that out-of-context reasoning improves with scale and is a plausible route to situational awareness, so larger models likely will act on descriptions in training data.
Report the combined source-reliability and task-following runs in an appendix as inconclusive, with full results and setup, and draw no conclusion about reliability from them.
Leave the unclear combined runs out of the paper and present only the clean source-reliability experiment as the main evidence for reliability-based recall.
Report results on every prompt format, using the simpler unseen formats without explicit reasoning as the headline and showing the engineered prompt only as an upper bound.
Use the single prompt engineered for the best test score as the default, and report its accuracy as the headline measure of the model's internalized knowledge.
Rewrite the descriptions as paraphrases that share no tokens with the target outputs, and measure whether the effect on predictions persists at similar size.
Accept the significant effect after the co-occurrence control as evidence of internalization and move on to the next experiment without further token-level checks.
Have a human label a random sample of completions as advice, refusal or other, then check that an automatic classifier agrees with those labels before computing the metric.
Classify completions with simple keyword matching on common refusal phrases such as an apology or inability statement, and count all other completions as advice.
